accessibility.seoDescription: How the {{governmentName}} portal works for people with disabilities, and how to report a problem.
accessibility.intro: This portal should be usable by everyone, including people who use screen readers, keyboard navigation, magnification or other assistive technology.
accessibility.standard: We aim to meet the <wcag>Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1</wcag> at level AA. The site is still being built, so some pages may fall short of that. We fix problems as we find them.
practices: A “Skip to main content” link is the first thing you reach with the Tab key.
Pages use headings, lists and landmarks so screen readers can move through them.
Images that carry meaning have text alternatives.
Menus, links and the search box can be used with a keyboard. Press Escape to close a menu.
Text can be enlarged to 200% with your browser zoom without losing content.
Pages declare their language so screen readers pronounce them correctly.
accessibility.plainText: Every service and government page is also available as plain Markdown text. Add .md to the end of a page address to open it. The sitemap lists every page on one screen, and llms-full.txt holds the full text of the site in a single file.
limitations: Charts on the Reports and Statistics dashboard can be hard to follow with a screen reader. The figures come from the city’s Full Disclosure Policy reports, which are linked from each section.
Some source documents published by the city are scanned PDFs without a text layer. We link to them as published and cannot change them.
The interface is available in Cebuano and English. Page content is still in English while translations are in progress.
accessibility.report: If something on this site is hard to use, or you need information in a different format, tell us. Include the page address and what went wrong. You can <issue>open an issue on GitHub</issue>.
